source_read: PDF, pp. 1795-1800 (all pages; text extracted with pdftotext -layout; every number used checked on pages rendered at 150 dpi, including Table 1, Table 2 and Figures 1-4)

claims.overstatement: None for the Marzuk part: the claim keeps association language, states the unadjusted day comparison and the unknown exposures, and correctly treats the cocaine-specificity reading and the homicide/traffic argument as the authors' readings. Two small precision points: (1) the 10 heat deaths whose dates helped set the 31.1 C threshold come from 1990-1995, so they overlap the 1993-1995 test years (their hottest date, 39.4 C, equals the hottest days of the test period, July 1995); the split-sample test is therefore not wholly independent of the threshold choice, which the claim could say. (2) 'Deaths from opiates without cocaine' is the paper's group 2, which also admits cocaine or metabolite in clinically insignificant amounts.
claims.note: Every Marzuk number in the statement and magnitude matches the printed page. Editors' calculations recomputed (Poisson, log rate ratio): cocaine 341/146 against 1667/949 days, RR 1.330 (1.183 to 1.494); opiates 118/146 against 675/949, RR 1.136 (0.934 to 1.382); ratio of the two 1.170 (0.932 to 1.469); expected hot-day cocaine deaths at the other-day rate 256.5, excess 84.5 (4.2% of 2,008). All as stated. Sensitivity check with the printed daily SDs instead of Poisson variance (cocaine variance/mean 1.21 on hot days, 1.07 on other days): cocaine 1.17 to 1.51, opiates 0.93 to 1.39, ratio 0.92 to 1.49, so the 'somewhat too narrow' caveat is right and the conclusions do not change. Percentages recomputed: 136/719 = 18.9%, 766/3919 = 19.5%, 12/126 = 9.5%, 71/689 = 10.3%, 10/40 = 25%, 10/48 = 20.8%.

anchors.locator: Table 1, cocaine overdose row, and table footnote
anchors.extracted: Cross-validation period 1 Jan 1993 to 31 Dec 1995, cocaine overdose deaths n = 2008: hot days 341 deaths, mean 2.34 a day (SD 1.68); other days 1667 deaths, mean 1.76 (SD 1.37); Mann-Whitney normal-approximation z = 3.98, P < .001. Footnote: a day is hot if its maximum hourly temperature or the preceding day's was at least 31.1 C (88 F); 1095 days, 146 hot and 949 other.

anchors.locator: Results > Fatal Unintentional Cocaine Overdoses, 1st to 3rd paragraphs (3rd continues on p. 1798)
anchors.extracted: 146 of 1095 days (13.3%) hot, 30 days at 35 C or more; 2008 cocaine overdose deaths, complete autopsy in 93%, mean age 39.0 (SD 8.8), 94.9% aged 15-54, 1569 men (78.1%). Hot-day mean 2.34 against 1.76 is a 33% increase in mean mortality; no significant differences in age, race, sex or place of death between people dying on hot and other days; autocorrelation of daily cocaine deaths 0.12 (P < .001), prior-day deaths explaining 1.4% of variance.

Hypothesis tested on 1993-1995 (cross-validation sample) after threshold set on 1990-1992; separate analyses for cocaine, opiate (not cocaine) and other-drug deaths; hot against other days compared with the Mann-Whitney test with day as the unit, plus an autocorrelation coefficient; no covariate, seasonal, weekday, holiday or trend adjustment described anywhere in the paper.

anchors.locator: Table 1, opiate overdose and other-drug overdose rows; with p. 1798, Results > Fatal Unintentional Overdoses of Opiates and Other Drugs, 1st paragraph, and Figures 3-4 (p. 1799)
anchors.extracted: Opiate overdoses (cocaine absent or clinically insignificant), n = 793: hot 118 deaths, 0.81 a day (SD 0.94); other 675, 0.71 (SD 0.86); z = 1.08, P = .28. Other-drug overdoses, n = 85: hot 12, 0.08 (SD 0.28); other 73, 0.08 (SD 0.28); z = 0.39, P = .69. Authors: no significant difference for either group and no discernible change at any temperature in Figures 3-4. Editors' recomputation: opiate RR 1.14 (0.93 to 1.38), not significantly different from the cocaine RR (ratio 1.17, 0.93 to 1.47).

Homicides 1993-1995: 4793, of which 4638 (96.8%) tested for cocaine, 902 positive; hot days 136 of 719 (18.9%) against other days 766 of 3919 (19.5%), chi-square 0.11, df 1, P = .69. Traffic deaths aged 15-54: 921, of which 815 (88.5%) tested, 83 positive; hot 12 of 126 (9.5%) against other 71 of 689 (10.3%), chi-square 0.01, P = .91. Authors read this as no rise in cocaine use in the population on hot days (abstract p. 1795; Comment p. 1799, 6th paragraph).

anchors.locator: Results > Fatal Unintentional Cocaine Overdoses, 4th and 5th paragraphs; Table 2
anchors.extracted: Among cocaine overdose deaths, opiates detected in 57.1% on hot days against 61.7% on other days; ethanol 42.9% against 41.4%; benzodiazepines 10.3% against 11.5%. Table 2: at least one drug commonly associated with hyperthermia risk in 20.3% (hot, n = 341) against 22.0% (other, n = 1667).

anchors.locator: Methods > Temperature Data > Sample of Hyperthermia Deaths That Involved Cocaine; Index Sample of Fatal Cocaine Overdoses; Establishment of the Threshold Temperature (continues p. 1797); Figure 1 (p. 1797)
anchors.extracted: 48 deaths certified as hyperthermia in 1990-1995 and not classified as unintentional overdoses; benzoylecgonine detected in 10, whose dates had daily maxima 17.2-39.4 C (mean 29.6, SD 6.1, median 30.9 C). Index sample 1096 days of 1990-1992 with 1382 cocaine overdose deaths: cumulative mean flat to 27.8 C, then rising, more steeply from 31.1 C. Threshold 31.1 C chosen from that median and plot, then tested on 1993-1995. The heat-death dates span 1990-1995, so they overlap the test years.

anchors.locator: Results > Deaths Due to Hyperthermia, 1st to 3rd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: 48 hyperthermia deaths 1990-1995 (34 male, 14 female; 3 infants, 29 aged 15-54, 16 over 54); 40 (83.3%) screened for benzoylecgonine and cocaine; benzoylecgonine in 10 (25% of screened, 21% of all 48), cocaine in 7 (17.5%, 14.6%); opiates in 1 of 40; ethanol in 5 of 41. Restricted to ages 15-54 (n = 27): 37.0% benzoylecgonine, 25.9% cocaine.

Authors list the 33% higher hot-day mean and call the association apparently specific to cocaine and not opiates; they add that only about 10% of days a year reach 31.1 C in New York City, so the temperature effect has no major influence on annual cocaine overdose mortality (consistent with the editors' estimate of about 85 excess deaths, 4% of 2008).

anchors.locator: Comment, 10th and 11th paragraphs (methodologic issues; closing paragraph)
anchors.extracted: Dose used before death unknown, so dose-temperature relation unknown; exact ambient temperature at the time of use unknown (night lows on very hot days stay in the 70s F); threshold set for the group, not individuals; whether decedents used occasionally or heavily unknown. Authors state it cannot be proved that high temperature directly raises the risk of death from cocaine use.
